skill.name: chrome-devtools
skill.description: Control Chrome through chrome-devtools-mcp for browser debugging, page inspection, screenshots, JavaScript evaluation, and network analysis.
skill.summary: Automate Chrome DevTools workflows from Claude Code or Codex.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily a Chrome DevTools MCP usage guide, not malicious code. Real risks come from copy-paste shell commands, runtime execution of chrome-devtools-mcp through bunx, process-killing cleanup commands, remote browser control, and screenshot capture of potentially sensitive pages.

remediation.issue: Runtime execution of latest external MCP package
remediation.suggestion: Pin chrome-devtools-mcp to a reviewed version and document verification steps before running bunx commands.
Replace pkill -9 examples with a safer shutdown flow, or clearly state that users must confirm the target process first.

remediation.issue: Browser content and screenshots may expose sensitive data
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings to avoid authenticated sessions, personal accounts, private pages, and production data when using screenshots or remote debugging.

remediation.issue: Remote debugging guidance can expose browser state
remediation.suggestion: Recommend loopback-only debugging, isolated profiles, and closing the debugging port immediately after use.

content.value_statement: Browser debugging often requires repeated manual checks across console logs, network requests, screenshots, and page state. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical command patterns for controlling Chrome through chrome-devtools-mcp.
actual_capabilities: Navigate Chrome to local or remote web pages through chrome-devtools-mcp.
Collect console messages and network request activity from a selected page.
Capture screenshots and text snapshots for visual and content inspection.
Evaluate JavaScript in the current page context for debugging tasks.
Automate basic page interactions such as clicking elements and filling fields.
Use isolated Chrome profiles to reduce browser profile lock conflicts.
limitations: Requires local installation of mcp tools and access to Chrome or a compatible browser.
Runs shell commands and external packages, so users should review commands before execution.
Screenshots and snapshots can expose private page content if used on sensitive sessions.
Some MCP CLI tools may require workaround parameters due to empty schema issues.

use_cases.title: Debug a local web app
use_cases.description: Open a localhost page, inspect console errors, and review page content during development.

use_cases.title: Investigate network behavior
use_cases.description: Navigate to a page and list network requests to understand failed calls or unexpected responses.

use_cases.title: Capture browser evidence
use_cases.description: Take screenshots and snapshots that help explain visual bugs or page state problems.

prompt_templates.title: Check a local page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Chrome DevTools MCP to open my local app and check the console for errors.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect page content
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target page with Chrome DevTools MCP, take a text snapshot, and summarize the visible page structure.

prompt_templates.title: Review network activity
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to the page, list network requests, and identify failed or suspicious requests with status details.

prompt_templates.title: Run a browser debug workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use one isolated Chrome DevTools MCP session to navigate, collect console logs, list network requests, evaluate a small JavaScript check, and capture a screenshot.

output_examples.input: Check the console on my local development page.
output_examples.output: The page opened in an isolated Chrome session. The console shows one application error and two warnings, with the error linked to a missing configuration value.

output_examples.input: Inspect why the login page is not submitting.
output: Found the submit button and form fields.
Observed a failed network request after submission.
Suggested checking the authentication endpoint response.

output_examples.input: Take a screenshot of the test page and describe it.
output_examples.output: A full-page screenshot was captured. The page displays a header, a main content card, and a footer, with no obvious layout overflow.

best_practices: Use isolated browser profiles unless you intentionally need an existing Chrome session.
Review shell commands before running them, especially cleanup and package execution commands.
Avoid authenticated or sensitive pages when collecting screenshots, snapshots, or network logs.
anti_patterns: Do not run browser debugging commands against private accounts without explicit consent.
Do not leave Chrome remote debugging ports open after the task is complete.
Do not paste secrets, session tokens, or production credentials into automated browser sessions.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps Claude-compatible tools drive Chrome through chrome-devtools-mcp for debugging, screenshots, console logs, and network inspection.

faq.question: Does it require command-line tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents mcp and bunx commands that must run on the local machine.

faq.question: Can it inspect local development sites?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include localhost workflows for console, network, and page snapshot debugging.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It can capture page screenshots, but users should avoid pages containing private or sensitive information.

faq.question: Why does it recommend isolated profiles?
faq.answer: Isolated profiles reduce browser lock conflicts and limit exposure from an existing personal browser session.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with production accounts?
faq.answer: Use caution. Browser automation can expose page content, screenshots, and network activity, so production or private sessions need explicit approval.
